### BUG-141 — Add-item search offers one catalog row at a fixed pack unit, so "1 roma tomato" can only be added as "1 lb roma tomatoes"

- **Date:** August 24, 2026 · **Surface:** grocery list add-item predictive search, mobile · **Found by:** Hans, BUG-134 device pass, item 6/7.
- **Symptom, plainly:** Hans wanted to add **one roma tomato**. The predictive search returned **exactly one selectable candidate — `1 lb roma tomatoes`** — and adding it wrote a new produce row in pounds. **There was no way to choose the count unit, no way to adjust the quantity at add time, and no way to add an item that is not already in the catalog.**
- **Three distinct defects wearing one symptom, and they should be separated at Phase 0:**
  1. **Only one candidate is returned** where the catalog demonstrably holds several roma-tomato rows (the duplicate groups in BUG-134 prove it). Either the search caps results or it filters harder than intended.
  2. **The unit comes fixed to the catalog row's pack** (`lb`), with no count-unit alternative offered — even though the very list being edited already carried `roma tomatoes` in **`each`**. ⚠️ **The two adds therefore land in DIFFERENT buckets, which is why item 7's same-bucket duplicate-add test could not actually be performed.**
  3. **No off-catalog add.** A user cannot type a free-text item the catalog does not know. ⚠️ **This is a real product gap for a grocery list — Extras are explicitly the user's own lane (D-WS9-183), and a lane that only accepts catalog rows is not that lane.**
- ⚠️ **Do NOT "fix" this by making the add path merge into an existing bucket.** That was ruled against in **D-WS9-183**: a user-added row legitimately sits beside a generated one, and the add route's lack of a bucket check is deliberate, not a defect.
- 🟡 **PARTIALLY CLOSED September 8, 2026 (Lane B, committed locally, DEVICE-UNPROVEN) — and the three defects came apart exactly as this entry said they would.**
  - ✅ **Defect 3 (off-catalog add) FIXED, CLIENT-ONLY.** 🔴 **THE LANE ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS UNREACHABLE:** `performAdd(null, text)` was there all along, but `handleAddItem` auto-picks `candidates[0]` whenever one is present — **so Hans typing "roma tomato" and getting exactly one row back had no route to it.** An always-present `Add "…" as typed` row now sits at the foot of the suggestions. ⚠️ **`emptyMessage` on the shared `TypeaheadList` is consequently dead for this consumer (`items.length` is never 0). Intended — a visible control beats a hint — and it changes no other consumer.**
  - ⚠️ **Defect 2 (unit fixed to the pack) MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED.** The row can be edited to `each` after adding, so the two adds can be merged by hand, **but the add path still takes the catalog row's pack.** Choosing it properly means knowing which alternatives the catalog row supports — **which is defect 1's question, so this closes when defect 1 does.**
  - 🔴 **Defect 1 (only one candidate) NOT FIXED AND NOT EXAMINED — CROSS-LANE, CORRECTLY REFUSED.** The client sends no limit; `GET /grocery-items/lookup?q=` alone decides how many candidates return, and that route lives in `artifacts/api-server/`, which the concurrent lane was actively editing. **CC stopped rather than absorbing it, and reserved no ID.** ⚠️ **"The catalog holds several roma-tomato rows" is still Hans's observation carried forward, NOT something anyone has confirmed in the route.**
- 🔴 **A NEW RISK THIS FIX CREATES, GATED ON THE DEVICE PASS AND NOT YET ANSWERED: making the free-text lane reachable may make CATALOG POLLUTION reachable with it.** **BUG-231's mechanism is the intake minting a typed name as its own catalog row.** If `performAdd(null, text)` writes to the shared `Ingredient` catalog rather than creating a personal extra, **every user typo becomes permanent product data every future user inherits** — which D-WS9-230's carve-out puts squarely in scope. ⚠️ **The device discriminator needs no DB access: add a nonsense name on one list, then search for it on a DIFFERENT list. Found = it minted a catalog row and this is a push blocker; not found = it correctly stayed an extra.**
- ✅ **DEFECT 3 DEVICE-PASSED, Android, September 8, 2026 — the `Add "…" as typed` row works.** 🔴 **AND THE CATALOG-POLLUTION RISK IS MEASURED AND CLEARED: a deliberate nonsense name (`zzqx test item`) added on one list did NOT come back when searched from a DIFFERENT list.** ✅ **So `performAdd(null, text)` creates a PERSONAL EXTRA, not a shared `Ingredient` row — making the lane reachable did not widen BUG-231. That was this block's only push-blocker candidate and it is closed.**
- **Status:** 🟢 **DEFECT 3 FIXED AND DEVICE-PROVEN · DEFECT 2 MITIGATED · DEFECT 1 OPEN, BLOCKED CROSS-LANE** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Target:** defect 1 rides with the next server grocery block · **Cross-ref:** BUG-124 · BUG-134 · BUG-140 · BUG-117 · **BUG-231** (the pollution mechanism) · D-WS9-183 · D-WS9-230.

### BUG-143 — `packsToCoverNeed` could not relate an oz need to an lb pack

- **Date:** August 25, 2026 · **Surface:** client render, `grocery.ts:329-372` · **Status:** ✅ **FIXED (local, unpushed) — device-verified item 8** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Cross-ref:** BUG-125 · BUG-146 · BUG-147 · D-WS9-186.
- **Symptom:** a weight need and a weight pack in *different tokens* could not be related — `packsToCoverNeed` returned `null` and fell through. 35 live rows, all `oz` → `lb`.
- ⚠️ **THE FACTOR WAS NEVER MISSING — IT WAS LEFT BEHIND.** `WEIGHT_UNIT_TO_GRAMS` (`ingredientConversions.ts:88-105`) has carried the constants server-side all along; **the render moved client-side in BUG-125/Root A and did not bring them.** That reframed the work from *author data* to *share a table*.
- **The fix:** four canonical tokens mirrored client-side (not the server's fifteen — `normalizeUnitToken` has already folded the rest), with `ingredientConversions.ts` named as source of truth per the hand-synced-mirror precedent in `lib/api/*`. The weight rule sits **ahead of** `packSizeHint`, because a direct weight relation is exact while the hint is parsed from authored prose.
- ⚠️ **IT CHANGES ZERO LIVE ROWS TODAY, AND CC MEASURED THAT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT.** Pre-change module extracted from HEAD, both composers run over all **2,061** live rows: **10 order lines change, all 10 from BUG-144, 0 from this.** Every one of the 35 rows needs ≤1 pack today. **Purely forward-looking — the D-WS9-186 shape exactly.** Device item 8 confirmed no visible change.
- **Pinned by three breaks**, of which ⚠️ **the good one is the DRIFT break: `lb` 453.59237 → 453.0, a 0.13% change, goes red at the 16 oz boundary — proving the constant's VALUE is pinned, not merely its presence.**
- **Two deliberate limits, now logged: BUG-146** (`fl oz` would misroute volume into the weight table) and **BUG-147** (weight need vs *container* pack still under-orders; pinned as guard W7).

### BUG-147 — A weight need against a CONTAINER pack still under-orders

- **Date:** August 25, 2026 · **Surface:** `packsToCoverNeed` · **Found by:** CC, **declined deliberately and pinned as guard W7 so the choice stays visible.**
- **Symptom:** BUG-143 relates weight↔weight but not a weight need to a pack expressed as a container carrying a weight — `"1 package (12 oz)"` against a **2 lb** need. ⚠️ **A real UNDER-ORDER, the ruled-worst direction.**
- **Why declined:** widening moves rows outside the measured 35-row population, and the scope guard's whole value was that 0 rows outside it changed. Needs its own before/after.
- **Likely shape:** `packSizeHint` already parses `"(12 oz)"`; the gap is relating that parsed weight through the gram table rather than only by token equality.
- 🔴 **IT IS A CLIENT BUG, AND CHAT-CLAUDE SCOPED IT INTO THE SERVER LANE BY MISTAKE (September 8, 2026).** The only fix site is `packsToCoverNeed` at **`artifacts/kiwi/lib/format/grocery.ts:466`** — the MOBILE tree. ✅ **A subagent verified independently that no server-side equivalent exists: `scalePurchaseForSubUnit` is ladder-only with no weight branch, and `totalBought` is weight-aware but is a RANKING criterion that never becomes an order quantity. The server passes the stored pack through unscaled.**
- 🔴 **THE 125-ROW / 14-UNDER-ORDER MEASUREMENT WAS MEASURING THE WRONG LAYER, AND CC CAUGHT IT WHILE FIXING THE TICKET (September 9).** **The server passes the stored pack through UNSCALED; the CLIENT scales it at render.** ✅ **So a population counted server-side counts under-orders THE CLIENT HAD ALREADY FIXED ON SCREEN.** **Both headline rows already scaled correctly before anything was touched: `crushed tomatoes` 28 oz vs `1 can (14.5 oz)` → 2 cans; `fresh baby spinach` 10 oz vs `1 container (5 oz)` → 2 containers. Guard W8 has pinned that path since BUG-143.**
- 🔴 **AND CHAT-CLAUDE HAD THE REFUTING EVIDENCE IN HAND AND EXPLAINED IT AWAY.** Hans's own screenshot shows that spinach row rendering as **`2 containers (5 oz)`**, and this entry recorded it as *"a different list instance, not this one."* **It was not a different instance — it was the client doing the arithmetic the server-side census could not see. §27.6 item 5 again, and this time the tell was a contradiction that was noticed and rationalised rather than followed.**
- ⚠️ **THE ORIGINAL FIGURE, KEPT SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT AS NEW: 125 rows / 14 "under-orders"** — `crushed tomatoes` 28 oz vs `1 can (14.5 oz)`, `crushed san marzano tomatoes` 28 oz vs `1 can (14.5 oz)`, `fresh baby spinach` 10 oz vs `1 container (5 oz)`, among others. ⚠️ **The other 111 are covered by a single pack — RIGHT BY LUCK, NOT BY ARITHMETIC, so the population is the exposure and 14 is only today's realisation of it.**
- ✅ **FIXED September 9 (mobile lane, LOCAL) — THREE NARROWER THINGS WERE GENUINELY BROKEN, none of them the headline:**
  1. **Same system, different spelling** — a need in `lb` against a hint in `oz` required an exact token match. 🔴 **This was old guard W7, which ASSERTED THE UNDER-ORDER AND SAID SO IN ITS OWN TEXT:** *"a real under-order… deliberately NOT fixed here… Pinned so the next person sees the choice was made."* ✅ **A guard that pins a DEFERRAL rather than a behaviour, and it worked exactly as intended — the assertion was updated, not worked around.**
  2. **Two-word units** — `(16 fl oz)` parsed the unit as `fl`.
  3. **Volume, entirely** — a weight table existed and no volume table did.
  Plus a measured unit leading the display (`1 lb block`, `purchaseUnit: "block"`), taking the precedence lesson from the server's `packMagnitude`, read as a reference only.
- **Rows that move:** same-system-different-spelling pairs · packs sized `N fl oz` · volumetric packs · packs whose measurement leads the display. **Rows that do NOT:** no stated size, and **any weight-vs-volume pair — that needs a per-ingredient density the client is never sent, and guard V6 pins the refusal with an absurd need so it cannot pass by luck.**
- ⚠️ **`quart` and `gallon` were added to `COUNT_NOUN_PLURALS` (`pint` was already there) because the volume work made those packs REACHABLE for the first time — without it, `2 quart` would have shipped as a NEW visible defect.** **A fix that makes a dormant path live owes a sweep of what that path now renders.**
- ⚠️ **POPULATION NOT RE-MEASURED.** The mechanisms were verified on constructed rows; **the 125 live rows were never enumerated, so how many of the 14 actually move is unknown.** **8 new guards V1–V8 plus the updated W7.**
- **Status:** 🟡 **FIXED IN THE WORKING TREE, DEVICE-UNPROVEN (mobile lane, September 9, LOCAL)** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Target:** done, pending a device pass · **Cross-ref:** BUG-143 · BUG-155 · BUG-138 (same misrouting) · BUG-117.

### BUG-150 — A recurring item and a meal need for the same ingredient collapse into ONE row, losing the meal's quantity

### BUG-157 — `neutral[600]` is used as body text in places where it fails AA contrast

- **Date:** August 25, 2026 · **Surface:** design tokens, app-wide · **Found by:** CC, while fixing BUG-154 — **surfaced as a scope question rather than silently widened.**
- **Symptom:** `neutral[600]` `#8A8474` measures **3.7278:1** on the white card. That **clears 3:1 for non-text UI** but **fails the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text.** It is the **LOCKED muted-text token**, read by roughly **20 placeholders** and — ⚠️ **critically — by real text, including meal descriptions at `MealRow.tsx:81-85`.**
- ⚠️ **TWO DISTINCT QUESTIONS WEARING ONE TOKEN, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE TRAP.** (1) **Placeholders** — arguably non-text UI, so 3:1 may be defensible; the counter-evidence is that **an outside tester missed a field entirely** (BUG-154). (2) **Body text at `neutral[600]`** — that is straightforwardly below AA and is not a matter of taste.
- ⚠️ **AND BUG-153's REUSE TARGET PROPAGATES IT.** `MealRow.tsx:81-85` is the pattern CC proposes reusing verbatim for the new subtext on two more screens (correct per §27.2). **Reusing it as-is ships below-AA body text on two additional surfaces.**
- **Three candidate dispositions, unruled:** change `neutral[600]`'s value (widest blast radius, and it is a locked token) · add a distinct **placeholder** semantic token at `neutral[700]` and repoint placeholders only (mechanical, leaves body-text uses untouched) · audit text-vs-non-text uses and move only the text ones.
⚠️ **MEASURED AGAINST THE LOCKED TOKEN FILE (chat-Claude, August 31 — computed from `design-tokens_4.ts`, full precision, both backgrounds):**

| foreground | on paper `#FBF7EF` | on white card | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neutral[600]` `#8A8474` (LOCKED muted) | **3.4886** | **3.7278** | non-text only; **fails AA for text on both** |
| `neutral[700]` `#6B5E4D` | 5.8956 | 6.2999 | passes AA |
| `neutral[800]` `#4A3F30` | 9.6107 | 10.2697 | passes; rejected at BUG-154 as too loud |
| `Palette.text.placeholder` `#A89A7A` | **2.5967** | **2.7748** | **fails even the 3:1 non-text floor** |

✅ **THE TWO FIGURES IN CANON WERE BOTH RIGHT AND ARE NOT A CONTRADICTION** — BUG-106's 3.49 is on **paper**, BUG-154/157's 3.7278 is on the **white card**. Recorded so nobody re-litigates it.

🔴 **A SEMANTIC PLACEHOLDER TOKEN ALREADY EXISTS AND IS WORSE THAN THE THING IT WOULD REPLACE.** `Palette.text.placeholder = '#A89A7A'` is defined in the locked file at **2.60:1 / 2.77:1** — below even the 3:1 non-text floor — while the ~20 live placeholders read `neutral[600]` instead. ⚠️ **THE TRAP THIS SETS: a sweep told to "repoint placeholders to the placeholder token" would make every one of them WORSE while appearing to fix them.** Any build here must set that token's VALUE, not merely point at it.
⚠️ **AND THE LOCKED FILE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS EXACT QUESTION:** `Palette.text.placeholder` says `#A89A7A` while `Components.tellKiwi.inputPlaceholder` says `Colors.neutral[600]`. **Two placeholder answers in one file** — the same one-mechanism-two-questions shape as `STAPLE_VARIANT_TO_BASE` (D-WS9-189).

⚠️ **THE COST ARGUMENT THAT SHOULD DRIVE THE DISPOSITION: the expensive half is IDENTICAL in all three options.** Every option requires enumerating and classifying each `neutral[600]` read as text vs non-text; only the trivial half (which colour each class lands on) differs. **Ruling for only placeholders (2) or only body text (3) pays that enumeration once and banks half the value, then pays it again later.**
⚠️ **WHAT OPTION 1 ACTUALLY COSTS, and it is a DESIGN consequence not a technical one:** `neutral[600]` is the quiet tier of a deliberate three-tier hierarchy (ink `neutral[900]` → secondary `neutral[700]` → muted `neutral[600]`). Raising it to pass AA lands it beside `neutral[700]`, **collapsing three tiers to two** — and it also darkens things that are meant to recede: the italic-dash section labels (`Components.sectionLabel.color`) and Cook Mode's dimmed next-step preview (`Palette.cookMode.nextPreview`). **A1 locked this value June 12; changing it is Hans's design call, not a technical one.**
- **Adjacent, same class, natural fold-in:** BUG-106's other half — `Palette.button.primary.text` on `terracotta[400]` measures **4.4273**, **0.07 under AA**, on the shared primary button.
✅ **RULED BY HANS, August 31, 2026 — THE HYBRID (options 2 + 3 together).** `neutral[600]` **KEEPS its value and its quiet-tier role** (section labels, Cook Mode's dimmed next-step preview, genuinely decorative muted UI stay exactly as designed — the A1 three-tier hierarchy is preserved). **Placeholders get a dedicated semantic token with a CORRECTED VALUE** — ⚠️ **not merely a repoint at the existing `text.placeholder`, whose `#A89A7A` is WORSE than what it replaces.** **Genuine body text moves to `neutral[700]`** (5.90 / 6.30 — the value BUG-154 already shipped for the one field Hans ruled on, chosen there over `neutral[800]` as *"just a bit darker, not super standout"*).
**Why the hybrid rather than 2 or 3 alone (the argument Hans ruled on):** the expensive half — enumerating every `neutral[600]` read and classifying it text vs non-text — is **identical in all three options**; only the trivial half differs. Ruling for one half banks half the value and pays that enumeration twice. **Option 1 was declined on its design consequence:** raising the locked token to pass AA lands it beside `neutral[700]` and collapses three text tiers to two.
**Build notes:** known text sites to move — `MealRow.tsx:81-85` (meal descriptions) plus BUG-153's two recorded sweep sites `PlanReviewMealRow.tsx:358` and `AddMealsSheet.tsx:341`. Resolve the locked file's self-contradiction in the same pass (`Palette.text.placeholder` vs `Components.tellKiwi.inputPlaceholder`). **Fold in BUG-106's other half** (primary-button text at 4.4273, 0.07 under AA). ⚠️ **The enumeration is the deliverable — every `neutral[600]` read classified, not just the ones already named here.**
- **Status:** 🟡 **RULED, unbuilt** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Target:** rides the mobile fix pass (the ruling lands now because BUG-153's reuse pattern is actively propagating below-AA body text to new surfaces) · **Cross-ref:** BUG-152 · BUG-153 · BUG-154 · BUG-156 · **BUG-106** (folded in).

### BUG-162 — Duplicate meals in My Meals

- **Date:** August 26, 2026 · **Surface:** Recipes → My Meals · **Found by:** chat-Claude, reading Hans's screenshot 2 — **not reported by Hans.**
- **Symptom:** *"Air Fryer Crispy Chicken Tenders with Honey Mustard and a Simple Green Salad"* appears **twice**, both `28 min · serves 4 · American`. A near-twin (*"…with Honey Mustard Dipping Sauce"*, 35 min) sits above them, so the catalog is also accumulating near-duplicates.
- ⚠️ **UNVERIFIED AS TO CAUSE — this is an observation from a screenshot, not a probe.** Two genuinely distinct meal rows, or one row rendered twice, are different bugs. **Establish which before designing anything.**
- ⚠️ **If it is two rows, it is the meal-level analogue of the ingredient-level fragmentation this whole arc has been unwinding**, and it matters more once wizard meals enter the shared catalog (see BUG-156).
- ✅ **CAUSE ESTABLISHED (Probe 1, August 26): distinct rows, no existing-copy guard on the clone path — and NOT historical.** Three distinct ids behind the screenshot (Hans's pair was created 3 minutes apart on July 12 — he was right about that pair, wrong about the general claim: **3 excess rows were created August 26 itself**, and the by-date breakout runs July 1 → August 26 with no stopping point). Population: **34 duplicate groups · 76 rows · 42 excess of 311 user meals.**
- **Mechanism:** `forkMealForUser → cloneMealInto` (`mealFork.ts:116-123`) deep-copies Meal + Dish + links + ingredients + steps and stamps `sourceStoreMealId: sourceMealId` — **and nothing anywhere reads it as a dedupe key** (two search shapes, one ignore-blind; the only near-hit is a comment). Proof row: pool meal `9e894ce4` forked twice, 30 days apart, the second on August 26. `dishFamilyKey` is no help — only `batch_generated` meals carry it.
- **Group anatomy: 16 groups are pure re-forks sharing one `sourceStoreMealId` (dedupable today, no schema change) · 18 involve a lineage-less wizard row (ties to BUG-156's catalog question) · 0 independent-generation collisions.**
- ✅ **FIX RULED (chat-Claude technical call, August 27): existence guard in `forkMealForUser` on `(userId, sourceStoreMealId)` — reuse the existing fork, including a previously customized copy** (matches what re-adding a meal should mean; Hans may override). The 42 historical excess rows stay per D-WS9-186. **Build follows Probe Block 2**, because the wizard-lineage half of the population depends on BUG-156's A4 answer.
⚠️ **SCOPE CORRECTION (Probe 2 audit, August 27) — THE RULED GUARD COVERS 16 OF 34 GROUPS, NOT ALL OF THEM.** Probe 2 established why the other 18 carry no lineage: they involve **live-generated** wizard meals, which by construction have no source store meal — and ⚠️ **the pool copy the publish path creates for them carries NULL `sourceStoreMealId` and NULL `dishFamilyKey` BY DESIGN** (`mealFork.test.ts:464`; see BUG-156). **A `(userId, sourceStoreMealId)` guard cannot see a NULL on either side.**
- ⚠️ **CANDIDATE MECHANISM FOR THE OTHER 18 — chat-Claude's audit, UNVERIFIED, and Phase 0 Q2 tests it:** a user's live-generated meal is published to the pool as an unlinked copy → that copy is later served back to **the same user** via store-fill → they fork it → **nothing can tell it is the meal they already have.** The test is whether each group's NEWER row carries a `sourceStoreMealId` pointing at a `live_writeback` meal matching its OLDER lineage-less twin. **If it holds, the fix needs a second identity signal, not a wider guard.**
- ⚠️ **THE CENSUS ALSO SIZES THE FORK POPULATION THE GUARD MUST COVER, AND CC LEFT IT UNREMARKED:** `batch_generated` 1,235 total / 1,124 public+catalog → **111 user-owned**; `live_writeback` 62 / 51 → **11 user-owned**. Those 122 rows can only be forks. Phase 0 Q3a confirms.
⚠️ **PHASE 0 SHARPENED THIS AGAIN, AND THE RULED GUARD IS NARROWER THAN EITHER PRIOR ESTIMATE: IT FIXES 16 OF 42 GROUPS AND *ZERO* OF THE 9 BOOMERANGS.**

**The census moved in ONE DAY** — user meals 311 → **359**, duplicate groups 34 → **42**, rows/excess 76/42 → **97/55**. Two of the five stamped boomerangs were created during the August 26 test run. ⚠️ **Any before/after measurement must pin a timestamp; this population is not static.**

**Three distinct mechanisms, now separated:**
1. **16 groups — re-forks** sharing one `sourceStoreMealId`. **The ruled `(userId, sourceStoreMealId)` guard fixes exactly these.**
2. **9 groups — the BOOMERANG, hypothesis CONFIRMED from both directions.** A user's live-generated meal is published to the pool 1–3s later by `publishMealToStore`, then **re-acquired by the same user** days later via store-fill. Direction A found 5 stamped instances with ids and timestamps; direction B enumerated all 51 pool meals independently and agreed exactly — **51/51 have a user-owned same-title parent 1–5s earlier, 0 orphans**, 5 stamped + 4 unstamped boomerangs (the 4 predate the `sourceStoreMealId` migration `20260724213633`, so they are provably forks with the column simply not yet written). **True boomerang population: 9 of 51 pool meals (17.6%).**
   - ⚠️ **WHY THE GUARD IS BLIND TO ALL NINE: in every boomerang the user's ORIGINAL carries `sourceStoreMealId` NULL** — it was live-generated, a fork of nothing. A guard asking *"do I already have a fork of this pool meal?"* correctly answers **no**. It cannot see the original.
3. **20 groups — a THIRD mechanism, and the largest bucket. See BUG-166** — it includes the very pair from Hans's founding screenshot (3 minutes apart, 2026-07-12).

**What identity signal exists today to link a live-generated meal to its own pool copy: none.** `sourceStoreMealId` is NULL on the pool copy **by design** (`mealFork.ts:212`; asserted `mealFork.test.ts:477`). `dishFamilyKey` is never written on any clone (0 hits in `mealFork.ts`; sole writers `mealMaterialize.ts:286` and `storeFill.ts:474`) and is NULL on all 97 duplicate rows. Title + `createdAt` proximity is the **only** thing that works — it matched 51/51 with zero orphans — but it is a heuristic, not an identity, and nothing in the product uses it. ⚠️ **The link exists in memory at `wizardActivation.ts:382`, where `publishMealToStore(tx, mealId)` holds the source id and receives the pool id — and persists neither direction.**

✅ **Negative claim re-verified two shapes at Phase 0:** nothing reads `sourceStoreMealId` as a dedupe key — query-shaped probe (`grep -B4 -A1 … | grep -ci 'where|findFirst|findUnique'`) returns **RAW COUNT: 0**, every one of 16 file hits classified.

- **Fix ruled (chat-Claude, August 27):** keep the `(userId, sourceStoreMealId)` guard for bucket 1, and for bucket 2 persist the discarded link as a **NEW column on the pool copy (`originUserMealId`)** — ⚠️ **NOT by overloading `sourceStoreMealId`**, which already means *"I was forked from this,"* is read by the rotation hop at `planningContext.ts:434`, and would be the line-824 two-sources-of-truth pattern (§10). Additive, so `mealFork.test.ts:477` stays true.
- **Status:** 🟡 **IN-PROGRESS — three mechanisms separated; ruled guard covers bucket 1 only; build deferred to the duplicate-meal block so `mealFork.ts` is opened ONCE with all three known** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Cross-ref:** BUG-156 · BUG-161 · BUG-163 · **BUG-166** · D-WS9-186.

### BUG-164 — The synthetic recurring-item bucket collides with the plan-derived row for the same ingredient

- **Date:** August 27, 2026 · **Surface:** grocery generation, `groceryList.ts:498` · **Found by:** CC, Phase 0, **while running down BUG-142's mechanism — surfaced against a chat-Claude hypothesis that was otherwise refuted.**
- **Symptom:** `whole milk` persists as **`1 each` AND `3 tablespoon`** — two rows, same ingredient — on **all seven** lists generated August 26. `bananas` and `lime` split the same way on three.
- ⚠️ **THE STATED MECHANISM IS REFUTED (build block, August 27). The `"each"` collision is UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION** — `buckets.has(norm|"each")` is only reached *after* the unit-agnostic name loop found no match, and any bucket at `norm|<anything>` necessarily has a `canonicalName` normalizing to `norm`, so that loop would have matched and continued. **The hard-keyed unit was never the cause.**
- ✅ **THE REAL CAUSE IS A CANONICAL-*NAME* MISMATCH**, verified against live prefs `["egg","milk","bread","coffee","Pet treats","Paper towels","Toilet paper","Bananas"]`: `milk` (pref) vs `whole milk` (plan) → synthetic `milk 1 each` on **7 of 7** · `egg` vs `large eggs` → synthetic `egg 1 dozen` · `Bananas` matches correctly on 5 lists and is **correct behaviour** on the 2 where the plan has no bananas.
- ⚠️ **AND `bread` vs `plain breadcrumbs` IS THE PROOF THAT NO MECHANICAL NAME RULE IS SAFE HERE** — absorbing that pair would be flatly wrong. **Fixing the name match requires ruling whether a recurring item ABSORBS a meal's need, which is D-WS9-188 and is UNRULED. CC stopped, correctly, per instruction.**
- ⚠️ **CHAT-CLAUDE'S CITED EVIDENCE WAS CONTAMINATED AND IS RETRACTED.** The `limes` and duplicate-`bananas` rows quoted when this entry was minted **do not reproduce from the current consolidator** — no lime pref exists for any list owner. They are **stale persisted rows from an earlier prefs state: the same contamination class as BUG-148.** All conclusions above are drawn from the live consolidator, not from persisted rows.
- **What shipped `dbd389e`:** the key/unit fix only, and it is **behaviour-neutral — differentially proven** by reverting it and re-running the consolidator: all **482 rows across 7 plans byte-identical**. ⚠️ **Break 6 stayed GREEN and the assertion was the exact tautology the brief warned against** (it recomputed the key from the row's own fields, so the break could not move it). **CC DELETED the test rather than leave something that looked like coverage** — the correct call, and it means this change is unpinned by design, evidenced instead by the 482-row differential.
- ⚠️ **THIS IS WHERE CHAT-CLAUDE'S REFUTED RECURRING-ITEM LEAD ACTUALLY LANDED.** The hypothesis was wrong about BUG-142 — it was not a recurring quantity — but a real recurring-item collision exists, one bug over. **Worth remembering as a shape: a wrong hypothesis can still be pointing at something.**
- **Relationship to D-WS9-188:** that entry owns the *design* question — how a recurring item SHOULD relate to a meal's need. **This is the mechanical defect underneath it.** Fix the collision; do not settle the design here.
⚠️ **RE-ATTRIBUTED AGAIN, August 28, 2026 — THE CSV DUMP DISPROVES THE NAME-MISMATCH THEORY FOR MILK. THERE ARE TWO MECHANISMS, NOT ONE.**
  1. ⚠️ **SAME ingredient, split by UNIT.** On list `6900ccc0`: `Whole milk` (0.5 **cup**) and `milk` (1 **each**, recurring) carry the **IDENTICAL `ingredientId` `d10747ca`.** **The name resolution WORKED — the ids match.** The rows never merge because the bucket key includes `unit`, and `each` cannot convert to `cup`. ⚠️ **This is the SAME shape as the `hot sauce` pair the conservation guard leaves standing — not a lookup failure at all.**
  2. **Genuinely different ids.** `eggs` (`ff985025`) vs `Large eggs` (`179e8716`); `bread` (`8e7dc0de`) vs `italian bread loaf` (`616b839f`). **These are the canonical-name mismatch CC diagnosed — and they are relationship 1 (synonym) or relationship 3 (distinct), which is D-WS9-189's job to tell apart.**
- ⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: a name-matching fix would not touch the milk case at all.** The synthetic recurring row is emitted at unit `each` under the preference's raw text, and buckets away from a resolved row of the same ingredient. **Any fix must reconcile the synthetic row's IDENTITY AND UNIT with the resolved ingredient, not just its name.**
- **Status:** ✅ **FIXED in code** (verified by TRIAGE-0's read-only check against `next`, October 16; not exercised live — the walk account had no recurring items). · *Previously:* 🔴 **OPEN — TWO mechanisms separated (unit-split on a shared id; and true id mismatch). Still blocked on D-WS9-188 for the design half.** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Cross-ref:** BUG-142 · BUG-148 · BUG-150 · BUG-165 · **D-WS9-188** · **D-WS9-189**.

### BUG-175 — Sixteen `IngredientAlias` rows are permanently unreachable, and one contradicts a Hans ruling

- 🟡 **PARTLY FIXED by grocery B1 (`b8c9e65` on `next`, DEV; ships with the post-approval deploy + the B1 data script):** the `coarse kosher salt --synonym-> kosher salt` row is now `distinct`, human-reviewed (the code-level never-fold veto already refused it). The 16 dead alias rows remain.

- **Date:** August 28, 2026 · **Surface:** `IngredientAlias` / `ingredientLookup.ts:104-118` · **Found by:** CC, D-WS9-189 Phase 0.
- **Symptom:** of 140 alias rows across 106 ingredients, **16 have an `aliasKey` that is ALSO some other row's `canonicalName`.** `lookupIngredientByName`'s ruled precedence is **canonical beats alias, unconditionally** — so step 2 is never reached and those 16 aliases can never resolve.
- **The inert set is almost exactly Hans's own cases:** `salt → kosher salt` · `sugar → granulated sugar` · `white sugar → granulated sugar` · `ground black pepper → black pepper` · `freshly ground black pepper → black pepper` · `cheddar cheese → sharp cheddar` · `egg → large eggs` · and 9 more.
- ⚠️ **THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR D-WS9-189: RELATIONSHIP 1 HAS BEEN ATTEMPTED BEFORE, BY SOMEONE, AND SILENTLY FAILED.** These rows are authored synonym assertions that do nothing. **A program that "just populates the alias table" would be repeating a move the catalog has already made and quietly lost.**
- ⚠️ **AND ONE OF THEM IS NOW WRONG BY RULING: `salt → kosher salt` contradicts Hans's August 27 call** that different salts are different products. **It is inert, so it causes no live defect — but it would become one the moment aliases were made reachable.**
- ⚠️ **STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE (D-WS9-189's Q2 answer): `IngredientAlias` maps a STRING to a ROW. Relationship 1 holds between TWO ROWS that both exist and are both referenced by dishes.** An alias can only express that by **deleting the loser row** — destructive, irreversible, and the BUG-096 pattern. **Right substrate for name→row; wrong substrate for row→row.**
- **Collision policy, verified:** silent **last-write-wins** at both writers — `prisma/seed.ts:566` upserts on `aliasKey` with `update: { ingredientId }`, and the BUG-096 merge script deliberately re-points. ⚠️ **No P2002, no skip — an authoring pass could silently steal an alias from a prior assertion with no error.**
- **Status:** 🟡 **PARTLY FIXED on DEV (grocery B1: the salt relation row) — the rest stays open.** *Census detail:* 🔴 **OPEN — REPRODUCED by the September 28 census (`f3f274a`, 20 fresh lists / 1,064 rows / 57 runs at HEAD `next`): 141 alias rows, exactly 16 dead (`salt → kosher salt`, `egg → large eggs`, `sugar → granulated sugar`, `lettuce → romaine lettuce`, `cheddar → sharp cheddar`, +11). 🔴 AND A RELATION ROW THAT CONTRADICTS A PERMANENT REFUSAL: `coarse kosher salt --synonym-> kosher salt` (medium, `ai_judge`, unreviewed) sits in `ingredient_relations`; D-WS9-217 says that pair NEVER folds. It is inert only because the confidence gate excludes it — a gate widening or a reviewer promotion breaks R6. Fix = flip the row to `distinct`, human-reviewed (a data row; the grocery pass carries it). `salt --subsumes-> kosher salt` (high) is the other contradiction already recorded here.** · **Priority:** **P3 (the salt row: fix with the pass)** · **Cross-ref:** BUG-096 · D-WS9-176 · D-WS9-177 · **D-WS9-189** · **D-WS9-217**.

### BUG-177 — Recurring "Milk" never matches the plan's `whole milk` bucket and appends a synthetic `1 each` row — ⚠️ **the mechanism behind 12 of the 31 duplicate groups**

- **Date:** August 28, 2026 · **Surface:** `groceryList.ts:500-502` (bucket match) → `:541-558` (synthetic append) · **Found by:** CC, D-WS9-188/189 program Phase 0. ⚠️ **FLAGGED, NOT FILED, BY CC — deliberately, because `groceryList.ts` and `ingredientConversions.ts` were reported mid-edit. Chat-Claude is filing it so it is not lost; the RE-VERIFY GATE below is mandatory.**
- **The chain, as read:** `normalizeIngredientName("Milk")` → `"milk"`. ⚠️ **There is no `milk` catalog row** — `"milk": catalogRow=NONE, alias→whole milk`. The bucket-match loop at `:500-502` compares `normalizeIngredientName(entry.canonicalName)`, which for the plan's row is `"whole milk"`, **and it does NOT consult `ingredient_aliases`.** So recurring `Milk` never matches, falls through to the synthetic append at `:541-558`, where `lookupPurchaseDefault("milk")` returns **null** (the code-table `milk` entry carries `gramsPerCup` only, no purchase pack) and the row is created as **`quantity: 1, unit: "each"`**.
- 🔴 **THIS IS THE COMMON PATH, NOT A CORNER: 6 of 13 users have `Milk` recurring, and `whole milk` has 211 dish references.**
- ✅ **IT EXPLAINS THE `milk 1 each` ‖ `Whole milk 3 tablespoon` SHAPE THAT IS 12 OF THE 31 DUPLICATE GROUPS** — and it explains the `each` unit, which had no other explanation. ⚠️ **The two rows share an `ingredientId` only because persist re-resolves it from the final name; the name split happens here, upstream.**
- ⚠️ **RELATIONSHIP TO D-WS9-188, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME THING.** D-WS9-188 is the ruled **product** question — how a recurring quantity and a meal need should be DISPLAYED together. **This is the mechanical reason they never met in the first place.** **Hans's ruling can be implemented correctly and these rows would still not pair up until this is fixed.**
- 🔴 **RE-VERIFY GATE — DO NOT BUILD FROM THIS ENTRY UNTIL IT PASSES.** Both implicated files were mid-edit by the BUG-174 + BUG-176 block when this was read, **and the `milk` code-table entry is exactly the kind of thing that block may touch.** ⚠️ **Re-read `groceryList.ts:500-502` and `:541-558` and re-run the `lookupPurchaseDefault("milk")` probe AFTER BUG-174/176 pushes, and quote both.** **Until then this entry is an UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS with strong evidence, not a finding.**
- ✅ **CORROBORATED August 28, 2026, INDEPENDENTLY AND BY ACCIDENT.** The fold-proof run measured `grocery.gap_fill_purchase_size` misses on a live consolidation: **6 misses, and ALL SIX are recurring synthetics with `ingredientId` NULL — `milk` · `bread` · `coffee` · `pet treats` · `paper towels` · `toilet paper`.** ⚠️ **`milk` having no `Ingredient` row at gap-fill time is exactly the mechanism this entry describes, observed from a different direction by a script that was not looking for it.** **The re-verify gate below still stands — this corroborates the mechanism, it does not re-read the two cited line ranges.**
- 🔴 **VERIFIED AND GENERALISED by the September 28 census (`f3f274a`, 20 fresh lists / 1,064 rows / 57 runs at HEAD `next`): 0 of 96 recurring rows across 20 lists carry a plan source — EVERY recurring item is a synthetic append, milk (11 of 20 lists), eggs, limes alike; there is no catalog row named `milk` (only `whole milk`). So D-WS9-188's annotated split ("5 lemons — 2 recurring + 3 for meals") is UNREACHABLE by this code path, not merely unbuilt: the match has to work before the display can exist.** Also seen: a recurring synthetic has `ingredientId: null`, skips the write-back by design, and is gap-filled FRESH on every generation — `1 package (6 rolls) paper towels` one run, `(6-pack)` the next (BUG-226's neighbour).
- ✅ **B3 Part A, September 29 (`150ce1f`) — mechanism confirmed and the fix RULED (D-WS9-284):** the match was exact equality against catalog canonicals, and no catalog row is named `milk`, `bread`, `eggs`, `limes` or `lemons`. Recurring text now resolves at every generation through the non-creating lookup. Dry run over the 20 census plans: 14 of 96 recurring rows meet a plan row, 40 carry a catalog id, 42 stay synthetic with stable hand-set packs; all 96 keep their recurring mark. Building in B3.
- **Status:** ✅ **FIXED on DEV — server half (grocery B3, `43dd340`…`5648033`; D-WS9-284): 16 recurring rows across the 20 census lists now meet the plan's row (whole milk 6, large eggs 4, lime 4, lemon 2); the phone's annotated render is grocery block C (C5).** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-188** · **BUG-164** · BUG-174 · BUG-175 · D-WS9-193.

### BUG-187 — Two rows on one list can share a reconcile `matchKey`, and only a flag filter keeps it from mattering

- **Date:** August 29, 2026 · **Surface:** `groceryReconcile.ts:111-119` `matchKey` · **Found by:** CC, reconcile safety audit — **as a latent hazard, not a live symptom.**
- **Observed:** list `93a03e23` carries **three** `Lime` rows, all `ingredientId=9741d311`, all unit `each`:

```
"Lime"   2 each  plan-derived   srcs=1   pack "2 limes"
"limes"  1 each  RECURRING      srcs=0   pack "1 lime"
"Lime"   1 each  USER-ADDED     srcs=0   pack null
```

- ⚠️ **`matchKey` returns `` `id:${ingredientId}|${unit}` `` — so all three produce the IDENTICAL key `id:9741d311|each`.** 🔴 **The key is not unique within a list, and the matcher assumes it is.**
- ✅ **HARMLESS TODAY ONLY BECAUSE RECONCILE SKIPS BOTH THE RECURRING AND THE USER-ADDED ROW**, so exactly one candidate ever reaches the matcher. ⚠️ **That is a filter, not an invariant. Change either flag's handling — which D-WS9-188's build will do — and two rows compete for one key with no defined winner.**
- 🔴 **D-WS9-188 IS THE TRIGGER, AND IT IS THE NEXT THING IN THE QUEUE THAT TOUCHES THIS.** Its whole job is to make the recurring row and the plan row relate to each other. **Read this entry before that build starts.**
- ✅ **CORROBORATED August 29, 2026, BY ACCIDENT AND FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION.** CC's BUG-181 regression harness initially reported `lime` and `lemon` collapsing — names that are in no fold map. ⚠️ **Cause: the harness fed PERSISTED rows straight to the merge, and a recurring row plus a user-added Extra CAN share a canonical name and unit in the table though they never do through the consolidator.** **Re-run with production bucketing as a pre-pass, the artifact vanished.** 🔴 **That is this entry's hazard reproduced in a harness — the collision is real in the DATA and is masked only by the code path, exactly as stated.**
- **Status:** 🔴 **OPEN — latent** · **Priority:** **P2, upgraded from P3 on the trigger** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-188** · BUG-177 · BUG-164 · BUG-126.

### BUG-188 — A measured need for a bunch-sold herb should buy a bunch, not sit in its own row

- ✅ **FIXED by grocery B1 (`b8c9e65` on `next`, DEV; ships with the post-approval deploy + the B1 data script):** every need converts through a per-ingredient pack yield, sums, rounds up; the ⅛-pack forgiveness applies to bunch-sold items only (Hans, September 28). Corpus: `1 bunch fresh cilantro (¼ cup)` + `(¼ bunches)` → `1 bunch fresh cilantro (¾ cup)`; cabbage 1 head + 2 cups → 2; iceberg 2 cups → 1 head.

- **Date:** August 29, 2026 · **Surface:** `groceryMerge` conservation guard / purchase resolution · **Found by:** Hans, reviewing the triage reference — **by disagreeing with a verdict chat-Claude had written as EXPECTED.**
- **What chat-Claude had ruled:** `cilantro 1 bunch` beside `cilantro 0.5 cup` is **correct as two rows**, because a bunch and a cup genuinely do not convert without per-ingredient data.
- 🔴 **HANS, VERBATIM, AND HE REFRAMED THE QUESTION:** *"1/2 cup cilantro doesn't really convert to a bunch. BUT I would argue that if you need a 1/2 cup or a cup of chopped cilantro or whatever cilantro, you should buy a bunch. so, in the example you provided, I would expect 2 bunches cilantro (1 bunch + 1/2 cup)."*
- ⚠️ **THE REFRAME IS THE FINDING: THE QUESTION IS NOT "HOW DO I CONVERT A CUP TO A BUNCH." IT IS "WHAT DO YOU BUY."** **A measured need for a herb sold in bunches resolves to a whole bunch — the conversion never has to be exact, because you cannot buy half a bunch.** ✅ **Same shopper-convenience principle the D-WS9-189 rubric now encodes: the test is what leaves the store, not what the arithmetic says.**
- 🔴 **BUT IT DOES NOT GENERALISE UNIFORMLY, AND A CRUDE VERSION OVER-BUYS.** Applying *"any measured need adds a pack"* across the board:

| Case | Crude rule gives | Right? |
|---|---|---|
| `cilantro 1 bunch` + `0.5 cup` | 2 bunches | ✅ Hans's ruling |
| `parsley 1 bunch` + `3 tbsp` | 2 bunches | ✅ same shape |
| `green cabbage 1 head` + `2 cup` | 2 heads | ❌ **one head is far more than 2 cups** |
| `white onion 1 each` + `1 cup` | 2 onions | ❌ probably over-buys |

- ⚠️ **THE DISCRIMINATOR IS YIELD PER PACK, WHICH IS EXACTLY D-WS9-189's `yieldQuantity` (D-WS9-194).** **A bunch of cilantro yields about a cup, so a cup demands a second bunch; a head of cabbage yields many cups, so it does not.** **Without that number the rule either under-buys herbs or over-buys produce.**
- ✅ **AND HANS GAVE THE TIE-BREAKER PRINCIPLE IN THE SAME MESSAGE, RULING ON `white onion 1 large`:** *"get a white onion and we're probably fine. if the user gets a small one and it's not enough they'll blame the grocery shopping more than the list."* ⚠️ **SO: a small under-buy is forgivable — the user blames the store. A gross over-buy is not, because the list is visibly wrong.** **Bias toward buying enough on small cheap items; do not round up large or expensive ones.**
- ✅ **CORPUS CASES from the September 28 census (`f3f274a`, 20 fresh lists / 1,064 rows / 57 runs at HEAD `next`) (the R2 tolerance is ruled against these):** `1 bunch fresh cilantro (¼ cup)` + `1 bunch fresh cilantro (¼ bunches)` — Hans's September 11 complaint verbatim, on plan `247cd7bb`; **61 rows across 20 lists are this class (16 foods), and the unloaded `pack_yields_REVIEWED.csv` covers 57 of them (13 foods) — missing: iceberg lettuce, rotisserie chicken, white onion.** ⚠️ The worst over-buy in the corpus is this class's inverse: **`4 heads iceberg lettuce (2 cup)` on 2 lists** — invisible to the over-order detector because each↔cup is unrelatable. ⚠️ Several "covered" yields are unit-incoherent (`fresh cilantro → 50 each/bunch`, `parsley → 1 cup/cup`) — coverage means a row exists, not that its figure is usable; the four with stated provenance are chives, ginger, the two cilantro parts and the two cabbages.
- **Status:** ✅ **FIXED on DEV (grocery B1, `b8c9e65`; production with the B1 data script after approval)** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-194** · **D-WS9-182** · **D-WS9-189** · BUG-142 · BUG-138 · BUG-251 (the duplicate-row list; cilantro is this entry, not that one).
- 🔵 **SEEN AGAIN September 11 (Hans, a new list): `1 bunch fresh cilantro` printed on TWO rows, from needs of 1/4 cup and 1/2 bunch.** Hans, verbatim: *"it should be one bunch one row"* — and *"I would overlook if it said 2 bunches."* **Consistent with the ruling: a bunch yields about a cup, so 1/4 cup + 1/2 bunch buys one bunch.** ✅ **TRACED (read-only lane, September 11 night):** one catalog row (`fresh cilantro`, default unit bunch, pack `1 bunch`); the two needs bucket as `cup` and `bunch`; the merge refuses because **`bunch` has no unit dimension** (neither volume, weight nor a count unit) and there is no ladder; the Sonnet pass then cannot accept a merge either (no common basis) — **so bunch + cup for one herb ships two rows on every path today.** Both rows wear the catalog's one-bunch pack, and the client composes the count per row. **A cup-per-bunch yield exists nowhere the runtime reads** — only in the reviewed but unloaded `pack_yields_REVIEWED.csv` (leaves 2 cup/bunch · chopped 1 cup/bunch · stems ½ cup), and keyed to the leaves/stems rows, not this one. **Two shapes sized, neither built:** (i) *same pack → one row, counts summed* needs no data but buys 2 bunches tonight (Hans wants one), 2 cabbages and 3 onions — exactly where his tie-breaker says no; (ii) *yield-based, rounded up* gives 1 bunch tonight and 2 for the ruled case, but a plain round-up still buys 2 cabbages for `1 head + 2 cup` and 3 onions — **so it needs the yield data AND a rounding tolerance, which is a ruling.** Since September 1: cilantro ×3, white onion ×2, yukon gold ×1, green cabbage ×1 (7 pairs, 14 rows). **Nothing ships before D-WS9-226's CSV load; the tolerance question goes to Hans with that block.**

### BUG-195 — The plan generator invents tags (`game day`, `season opener`) into an open, unfilterable field that feeds TWO AI inputs and one rendered card label

- **Date:** September 1, 2026 · **Surface:** wizard candidate tags → `Meal.tags` / plan-template tags · **Found by:** Hans, BUG-190 device pass item 1.
- **Symptom, verbatim:** *"it added 'game day' as a tag and 'seaon opener' or something else like that on my first try. we don't have a 'game day' tag... I want to be sure AI isn't generating things users can't filter on."*
- ⚠️ **HIS CONCERN IS RIGHT AND UNDERSTATED — THERE IS NO TAG VOCABULARY AND NO TAG FILTER AT ALL.** Verified in the August 4, 2026 Phase 0 (retained in D-WS9-100 as the standing reference on `tags`): `Meal.tags` (`schema.prisma:530`) and `Dish.tags` (`:436`) are open `String[]`, validated only at `max(10)` items × `max(40)` chars — **no enum, no closed set**. 🔴 **AND THE "SEARCH MATCHES TAGS" BELIEF IS FALSIFIED — no text search on meals or dishes exists.** PRD §9.6 (LOCKED) and §9.3.3 describe a tags-inclusive search that was never built. **So today NO tag is filterable, not just the invented ones.**
- 🔴 **THE HARM IS NOT DISPLAY — IT IS FEEDBACK. THREE LIVE NON-SEARCH CONSUMERS READ `tags`:**
  1. **Find-Similar's AI input** (`findSimilar.ts:25`, `SwapMealSheet.tsx:98,243`) — ⚠️ **and BUG-058 is open on that surface, so a novelty tag changes an unfixed bug's inputs.**
  2. **The plan-generation shortlist** (`storeShortlist.ts:316`) — so an invented tag re-enters generation.
  3. **The Featured/Tried-&-True rail label** (`triedTrue.ts:61`) — ⚠️ **which renders `tags[0]` directly. A user can see a home-screen card labelled `game day`.**
- ⚠️ **THE LOOP IS SELF-REINFORCING: AI emits a novelty tag → write-back persists it → the shortlist surfaces it → the next generation copies it.** **This is exactly the "divergence generator" D-WS9-109 named — arriving from the AI side. The ruling that killed user-typed tags (D-WS9-100/-101) never covered AI-emitted ones, so nothing guards this direction.**
- ✅ **AND THE UNDERLYING BEHAVIOUR IS A KEEPER — HANS REVERSED HIS OWN SKEPTICISM ON DEVICE ITEM 10: *"the NFL opener comment came up again, and honestly I think it's a good feature even if I was skeptical at first."*** 🔴 **SO THE DEFECT IS THE CHANNEL, NOT THE CONTENT. Seasonal and timely awareness belongs in PROSE — `whyBullets`, the meal description — where it is read once and consumed by nothing. It does not belong in `tags`, a field with three machine consumers and no vocabulary.** ⚠️ **Any fix that suppresses the timeliness rather than redirecting it is the wrong fix and Hans will reject it.**
- 🔴 **UNVERIFIED — CHARACTERISE BEFORE DESIGNING ANYTHING.** Hans saw these on a plan-candidate card. **Whether candidate/plan-level tags PERSIST (to `MealPlanTemplate`, or to `Meal.tags` via the live write-back path) or are ephemeral to the card is unestablished, and it decides both the blast radius and the fix.** Establish it first; the three-consumer harm above only fires if they persist.
- ⚠️ **§27.2 REUSE CHECK BEFORE ANY BUILD: D-WS9-109 already owns "typed attributes that generation READS, instead of user tags nothing consumes."** This is plausibly a rider on that, not its own feature. **And D-WS9-109's own sequencing rule applies directly here: ask what READS a field before building what writes it.**
- **Status:** 🔴 **OPEN — needs characterisation** · **Priority:** **P2 — pre-beta under D-WS9-174** (a mislabelled home-screen card is a *"why does it say that"* item; the Find-Similar contamination is silent and worse) · **Target:** a read-only characterisation rider on the next plan-generation or catalog block · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-109** · **D-WS9-100 / D-WS9-101** (the tags Phase 0 and the decline) · **BUG-058** (open, on consumer 1) · BUG-190 · D-WS9-200.

### BUG-205 — Store-bought products live in `Dish.substitutions` JSON and NO allergen mechanism reads them — ✅ RULED by Hans, September 14, 2026 (option C, scoped down); UNBUILT

- **Date:** September 5, 2026 · **Surface:** `Dish.substitutions` (JSON) → every allergen-filtered surface · **Found by:** CC, ingredient-rollup Phase 0, **while measuring something else.**
- **Status:** ✅ **RULED September 14, 2026 — UNBUILT.** · **Priority:** 🟡 **P2, DOWNGRADED FROM P1 BY THE RULING** — the filter Hans named runs BEFORE substitutions exist, so the exposure is far narrower than the raw numbers below suggest · **Target:** the WS9B store-bought toggle lane, which is where Kiwi itself starts offering swaps · **Cross-ref:** **BUG-121** · D-WS9-211 · D-WS9-174 · D-WS9-175.
- **Measured:** **1,517 dishes** carry substitutions · **660 distinct product names** · **614 have no matching `Ingredient` row at all** · **147 would derive ≥1 allergen token today** if anything looked at them (*sour cream, Italian-style breadcrumbs, pre-shredded mozzarella, store-bought pizza dough*).
- 🔴 **THE DERIVATION WALKS `meal → dishLinks → dishIngredients → ingredient`. SUBSTITUTIONS ARE NOT ON THAT PATH.** Neither today's stamping nor the proposed ingredient rollup sees a single one of them. **This is not a gap the rollup introduces or closes — it is orthogonal to that decision, and it is larger than the AI tail the rollup was proposed to eliminate (147 vs 110).**
- ⚠️ **IT IS BUG-121's BLAST RADIUS, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** BUG-121 says dual-path dishes render both paths because `pathKey` is unread. **This says the store-bought path is also unstamped.** A user on the bought path can be served a dish whose allergens were computed entirely from the scratch path's ingredients.
- ⚠️ **UNVERIFIED, AND IT DECIDES THE PRIORITY: whether those 147 product names reach a user-visible surface at all.** CC measured the JSON, **not its consumers.** `DishIngredient.pathKey` is null on all 36,293 rows, so the bought path may be inert today. **If it is inert this is P3 latent; if any surface renders it this is a live P1 of exactly BUG-201's class. Measure the consumers before scoping anything.**

---
- ✅ **RULED BY HANS, September 14, 2026 — option (c), and his reasoning RESHAPES the problem rather than just picking a branch. Verbatim:** *"the allergen filter is when meals are suggested to users. so the filter runs before they get a meal they can adjust to store-bought ingredients/mixes/elements. once the user goes to the store and actually orders the food it’s out of our hands, we just don’t want to look stupid telling someone with a shellfish allergy to make baja shrimp tacos. and ‘not checked’ could be implied or included in the T’s&C’s unless it makes the feature feel more powerful and reliable to have it note that we didn’t evaluate what’s in a package."*
- 🔴 **WHAT THIS SETTLES: THE ALLERGEN MECHANISM DOES NOT NEED TO READ `Dish.substitutions` AT ALL.** The filter’s job is the MEAL, at suggestion time, before any substitution exists. **A user adapting a already-safe meal to a store-bought element is downstream of the promise Kiwi makes** — and the promise is "we will not suggest you a dish you are allergic to", not "we have audited every package in your grocery store". ✅ **So the 614-products-with-no-Ingredient-row number below is NOT a 614-item backlog; it is context for a feature that does not exist yet.**
- ⚠️ **CHAT-CLAUDE’S CALL ON THE ONE SEAM HANS’S FRAMING DOES NOT COVER, made under standing delegation — HANS OBJECTS IF HE DISAGREES: the distinction is WHO OFFERS THE SWAP.** A user reaching for a taco kit on their own is out of our hands, exactly as ruled. **But WS9B’s store-bought toggle is KIWI offering the swap** — and an app that surfaces "use a store-bought pizza crust" to a coeliac user is making a suggestion, not observing one. ✅ **RULED: where KIWI offers the swap, the offer carries a short, plain line at the point of offer that the package’s contents are not allergen-checked — NOT buried in the T&Cs.** Hans left this door open himself (*"unless it makes the feature feel more powerful and reliable"*) and **it does: for an allergy audience, saying plainly what you have and have not checked reads as careful, not as weak.** One line, at the offer, is the whole treatment.
- ✅ **HANS REFINED IT THE SAME DAY, and his version is better than chat-Claude’s — THIS IS THE RULING: the line is a SUBTLE footnote, *"* Kiwi does not evaluate store-bought items for allergens"*, and it renders ONLY IF THE USER HAS INDICATED AN ALLERGY OR AVOIDANCE** (the allergy + avoidance chips or the free-text field). 🔴 **The conditional is the whole point: a blanket disclaimer on every store-bought swap trains everyone to ignore it, and it makes the app look nervous to the ~most users who have no allergen set. Shown only to the people it is for, it reads as precision rather than as a hedge.** ⚠️ **So the treatment has a PRECONDITION: it needs the user’s allergen/avoidance state at the point the swap is offered. Confirm that state is available on that surface before building — if it is not, the footnote is not buildable as ruled and that is a finding, not a licence to show it unconditionally.** *(Chat-Claude’s earlier version — an unconditional line at the point of offer — is superseded; the seam it identified stands.)*
- ✅ **HANS ANSWERED THE PRECONDITION THE SAME EVENING, AND RE-PRIORITISED: the allergen indication comes from the WIZARD. A standing allergy lives in preferences and hydrates from the profile; the user can ADD or OVERRIDE per plan** — *"if, for example, this week they have a guest who has an allergy."* **So the state the footnote keys on is the plan’s effective allergy/avoidance set (profile-hydrated + this-plan overrides), not the profile alone.** 🔵 **And his priority call, verbatim: *"I honestly view this as P2 and it could go after launch."* P2 confirmed; NOT on the launch path.**
- 🔵 **THEREFORE THE BUILD IS SMALL AND IT BELONGS TO WS9B, NOT TO THE CORRECTNESS BLOCK:** no allergen derivation over 660 product names · no `Ingredient` rows for the 614 · no name-derived stamping (⚠️ **D-WS9-211: allergen stamps are name-derived and the false-positive class RECURS; `Ingredient.category` is not a usable cross-check — `vegan butter` is filed as Dairy. Do not propose it again**) — just the one honest line where Kiwi offers a swap.
- ✅ **AND THIS CLOSES THE CORRECTNESS BLOCK’S SECOND OPEN RULING.** Only D-WS9-238 remained beside it, and that was ruled the same day.

### BUG-213 — Cilantro cannot pool: no bunch↔cup figure exists anywhere

- ✅ **FIXED by grocery B1 (`b8c9e65` on `next`, DEV; ships with the post-approval deploy + the B1 data script):** stems and leaves are co-harvested parts that ride free with the bunch; three cilantro rows → one bunch, the need untouched.

- **Date:** September 6, 2026 · **Surface:** the component pool's `toYieldUnit`; catalog row `fresh cilantro` · **Found by:** CC, D-WS9-189 A3, while the pool was being opened.
- **Status:** ✅ **FIXED on DEV (grocery B1, `b8c9e65`, with BUG-188)** · **Priority:** **P2** · **Target:** BUG-188's ruling — an instance of it, not a separate fix · **Cross-ref:** 🔴 **D-WS9-189** · **D-WS9-222** · BUG-208 · D-WS9-218.
- 🔴 **THIS IS THE ROW HANS STOPPED THE SEPTEMBER 6 DEVICE PASS ON, AND A3 DID NOT CLOSE IT.** List `bd29f91a` still ships three lines: `1 bunch fresh cilantro (1⅓ cup)` · `1 bunch fresh cilantro stems (¼ cup)` · `1 bunch fresh cilantro leaves (½ cup)`.
- **Why:** `fresh cilantro` is authored in **cups**; the component basis is **bunch**; cilantro's `conversionRef` carries `gramsPerCup: 16` but **no grams-per-bunch**. Converting cups → bunches is therefore undefined.
- ✅ **THE POOL DECLINES, AND DECLINING IS CORRECT.** Emitting the twin — two rows both named `fresh cilantro` — is worse than leaving three honest rows. **This is BUG-208's guard working as designed, not a new failure.**
- ⚠️ **CC did NOT invent a grams-per-bunch figure, which is exactly what A1 did and is why 95 edges shipped unverified.**
- 🔴 **CORRECTED September 6, 2026, HOURS AFTER THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN — AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. THE CONVERSION IS NOT NEEDED AND HANS ALREADY RULED SO, IN BUG-188 ON AUGUST 29.** His words there, verbatim: *"1/2 cup cilantro doesn't really convert to a bunch. BUT I would argue that if you need a 1/2 cup or a cup of chopped cilantro or whatever cilantro, you should buy a bunch. so, in the example you provided, I would expect 2 bunches cilantro (1 bunch + 1/2 cup)."*
- ⚠️ **BUG-188's own headline says THE QUESTION IS NOT "HOW DO I CONVERT A CUP TO A BUNCH" — IT IS "WHAT DO YOU BUY." A measured need for a herb sold in bunches resolves to a WHOLE BUNCH, and the conversion never has to be exact because you cannot buy half a bunch.** **So the fix is `ceil` to whole bunches and sum, NOT a grams-per-bunch figure. BUG-188 is RULED AND UNBUILT; this entry is a live instance of it, not a new problem.**
- 🔴 **AND THE PROCESS FAILURE IS AN EXACT REPEAT, ONE WEEK APART.** BUG-188 exists because chat-Claude ruled `cilantro 1 bunch` beside `cilantro 0.5 cup` **"correct as two rows"** and Hans overturned it. **On September 6 chat-Claude wrote that the pool's decline was "correct" and that the fix was a catalog figure — the same wrong verdict, on the same food, for the same reason: it treated an unconvertible unit as the problem instead of asking what the shopper buys.** ⚠️ **Cause both times: scoping from what the code/report said rather than searching canon for an existing ruling. `project_search` finds BUG-188 in one call.**

- 🔴 **THE ACTUAL MEASUREMENT, September 9, Neon branch, ONE plan, THREE runs, THREE DIFFERENT BEHAVIOURS, all at temperature 0:**

| run | rows | garlic |
|---|---|---|
| warm-up | 65 | 3 rows, **no refusal** — the model echoed all three, so the passthrough shortcut ran |
| A | 65 | 3 rows, **refused** (`neededGrams: 16`, `returnedGrams: 17`) |
| B | **63** | **merged** to 16 clove / 2 heads, all three `sourceKeys` |

- ⚠️ **A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DIVERGENCE IN THE SAME SET, AND IT IS NOT GARLIC: `paper towels` came back `1 package (6 rolls)` on the warm-up and `1 package (6-pack)` on run A.** **Gap-fill divergence at temperature 0 — or a write-back that had not committed before the next read. NOT DIAGNOSED.**
- 🔴 **SETTLED September 9, 2026, AND CHAT-CLAUDE'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. 12 runs, two independent replications (3 write-back ON + 3 OFF, twice).**
  - **`promptHash` IDENTICAL in all 12** — the full request hashed: system, messages, model, `temperature: 0`, `max_tokens`. **The input never moved, in either phase.**
  - 🔴 **SIX DISTINCT `outputHash` VALUES FROM TWELVE IDENTICAL PROMPTS.** Modal 6/12, another 2/12, four singletons; raw length 4089–4490. **The model is not deterministic at temperature 0.**
  - ✅ **The catalog fingerprint was UNCHANGED across all 12 (the catalog is warm, so the write-back had nothing to move) and suppressing the write-back entirely changed nothing.** **The write-back is not the variance source; it cannot be.**
- ✅ **AND THE VARIANCE DOES NOT REACH THE USER AT HEAD: `rowsHash` IDENTICAL across all 6 runs of the second experiment, despite 4 distinct raw outputs. The model varies PROSE AND FORMATTING, not the substantive numbers.**
- 🔴 **THE REFRAME, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE THIS ARC HAS PRODUCED — CC's, replacing its own earlier "a refusal is a deterministic sink": MODEL OUTPUT VARIES ALWAYS; IT REACHES THE USER EXACTLY WHEN THE VARIATION CROSSES A GUARD'S DECISION BOUNDARY.**
  - **At HEAD the garlic group refuses UNCONDITIONALLY — no boundary, so no visible variance.** **Last block's 65/65/63 happened because the basis change put that group onto a CONSERVATION BOUNDARY where 16 conserves and 17 does not, and the model's arithmetic noise straddles it.**
  - 🔴 **SO BUG-214 IS NOT "MAKE GENERATION DETERMINISTIC" — THAT IS NOT ACHIEVABLE AND IS EXPECTED INFERENCE BEHAVIOUR, NOT OUR DEFECT. IT IS "A GUARD BOUNDARY MUST NOT SIT WHERE THE MODEL'S NOISE LIVES."**
  - ⚠️ **THAT IS A LIVE DESIGN CONSTRAINT ON BUG-241's FIX AND ON EVERY FUTURE GUARD: any change that converts an UNCONDITIONAL refusal into a CONDITIONAL one makes model noise user-visible.**
- 🔵 **`paper towels` IS ACCOUNTED FOR AND IT IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM.** **Zero catalog rows match it; all 6 live grocery rows carry `ingredientId: null` and `isRecurringItem: true`.** **It is synthetic, skips the write-back by design, and is gap-filled fresh on EVERY generation forever — it can never be cached.** **Its variance is Haiku's `gap_fill_purchase_size`, not `generate_list`: 5/5 stable inside one burst, but THREE distinct answers across a day, two of them already persisted onto live rows.** ⚠️ **This is BUG-124 / D-WS9-226's null-`ingredientId` population, now with a measured consequence.**
- 🔵 **SUPERSEDED — chat-Claude's write-back hypothesis, kept because the refutation is the value:** `fillPurchaseSizesWithWriteBack` mutates the catalog DURING generation, so run N+1 reads a different input than run N and the prompt is not actually identical. **The paper-towels difference is the shape that fits it.** ⚠️ **TESTABLE IN ONE PROBE: repeat the same plan with the write-back disabled, or against a freshly branched catalog each time. Do not adopt it because I proposed it.**
- ⚠️ **THE ORIGINAL FIX STANDS — pinning to 0 was correct and necessary. What is refuted is the claim that it was SUFFICIENT.**

- 🔴 **SCOPE WAS WIDER THAN THE ENTRY IMPLIED: `"garlic cloves": "garlic"` sits in `MERGE_GROUP_VARIANT_TO_BASE`, which applies under `EMPTY_RELATION_INDEX` — so this reached EVERY user, including one with no relation data loaded.** It was never conditional on the relationship program having run.

- 🔴 **CHAT-CLAUDE'S PRESCRIBED FIX WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE MADE THINGS WORSE.** The prompt said re-key conservation to the folded group name. **Grams is the guard's basis, a subUnit child is deliberately NOT gram-convertible (`clove` → null), and `head` is not a count unit — so re-keying alone turns EVERY garlic group into `not_convertible` and refuses it wholesale, including the correct merges BUG-215 ships.** ✅ **What landed instead: a SECOND basis that sums in child units exactly as `mergeGroup`'s own subUnit branch does, with both sides always using one basis or neither.**
- ✅ **Four changes: group-keyed conservation · the sub-unit basis · exact-name-then-fold matching (row-for-row echoes stay byte-identical) · and a structural backstop — every `aiSubset` entry is popped, absorbed, refused or rebuilt, with no fifth path.** ⚠️ **`leftoverIndices` is GONE: its only remaining job was handing a dropped row's slot to a row the model invented, which is how the drop stayed invisible.**
- 🔴 **THE "THREE RUNS, 65/65/65 IDENTICAL" MEASUREMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS EVIDENCE OF DETERMINISM — CC RETRACTED IT AGAINST ITSELF on September 9.** **A refusal is a deterministic SINK: whatever the model returns, the rebuild emits the same rows. The identity was the GUARD's, not generation's.** ✅ **It stays valid for what it actually shows — BUG-217's fix produces a STABLE OUTPUT — and that is worth keeping.** 🔴 **It is NOT evidence for BUG-214, and the position block carried it as such until corrected.**
- ✅ **AND A TRUE A/B AGAINST THE PRE-FIX SOURCE on the same branch, same plan, warm catalog — the strongest single result in the block: 64 rows → 65.** **Pre-fix shipped `garlic cloves 15 clove` against pack `1 head of garlic` — ordering 10 cloves for a 15-clove need, a 33% UNDER-ORDER, with two source buckets silently dropped.** Post-fix refuses the merge and ships the full need in two rows, and **logs the refusal** (`grocery_ai_merge_refused`, `canonicalName: "garlic"` — the FOLDED key, `inputRows: 3`, `basis: "sub_unit_children"`).
- ⚠️ **THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR BUG-214, NOT CLOSURE OF IT.** A ≡ B says BUG-217 rather than sampling was the divergence; **but the stored September 7 list's 63 rows came from OLDER code that was never re-run, so the 65-vs-63 pair is not proven to be one mechanism.** One plan, one branch, one evening, temperature 0.
- 🔴 **AND THE GUARD CAUGHT THE MODEL DOING ARITHMETIC ACROSS INCOMPATIBLE UNITS — a second defect class the drop was hiding.** On list `cb5c8f6e` the consolidated inputs are **6 each + 9 clove + 1 head**, and the model returned **16**: `6 + 9 + 1`. ⚠️ **It summed a HEAD as one CLOVE.** True need is `6 + 9 + 10 = 25` cloves. ✅ **Post-fix the guard refuses that merge, the three parts ship separately each carrying a head pack, and the shopper buys 3 heads for a 25-clove need — OVER, not under.** ⚠️ **CC flags "the model summed a head as one clove" as an INFERENCE: `6+9+1 = 16` fits exactly and no other decomposition does, but the model never said so.**
- 🟠 **THE USER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT NEEDS A DEVICE LOOK: a refusal ships THREE garlic rows on one list** (`garlic cloves`, `garlic`, `garlic head`, plus `garlic powder` separately). **Safe, and it looks broken.** ✅ **The cure is the basis change described below, which BUG-138 has now unblocked.**
- 🔴 **THE TRAP FOR THE NEXT BLOCK, AND IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. The garlic group is now REFUSED rather than merged, because `conversionForGroup` picks whichever member resolves first — here the ladder-less `garlic cloves` row.** **Making the basis see the ladder would let it merge to 15 cloves — and the pack would STILL read `1 head of garlic`, because the pack ladder is BUG-138's separate fix. That converts a SAFE REFUSAL into a SILENT UNDER-ORDER.** 🔴 **The basis change and BUG-138's ladder resolution must land TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL.** ✅ **CLEARED September 8, 2026: BUG-138 LANDED as `bd2590e`, so the basis change is now SAFE and is the next block's obvious work — it is what collapses the three garlic rows into one correct row. CC declined to take it in the same commit and was right to.**
- 🔴 **THE MECHANISM, IN CC'S WORDS AND WORTH KEEPING:** the AI echoes a merged line under one name; `entriesByName` keys on the raw name, so **a two-row cross-name fold gives each entry a length < 2 and BUG-142's conservation guard skips both.** The unechoed source is never popped from the queue, then finds no host in the `absorbedKeys` loop **because that loop also matches on the unfolded name** — so its quantity and its provenance vanish from the list with nothing raising a flag.
- ⚠️ **THIS IS A BETTER EXPLANATION FOR BUG-214's 65-vs-63 THAN SAMPLING IS, AND IT WOULD SURVIVE THE TEMPERATURE PIN.** `a9fb3b9` removed the sampling source; it did not prove sampling was the cause. **Do not close BUG-214's reproducibility question until this is fixed and a repeated run is measured on a Neon branch.**
- ⚠️ **THE GUARD'S BLINDNESS IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: BUG-142 conserves quantity WITHIN a name and cannot observe a fold ACROSS names.** Every fold mechanism shipped since — the synonym reader, the component pool, the subsumes work — moves rows across names. **A guard scoped to the pre-fold key cannot police post-fold behaviour, and this is the second time that shape has bitten (BUG-215 was the first, on survivor identity rather than membership).**

### BUG-218 — The ladder asks for a conversion the row already states: 39 live rows carry the mass in `purchaseDisplay` and are still reported as gaps

- **Date:** September 7, 2026 · **Surface:** the subUnit/ladder gap detection — it fires whenever need-dimension ≠ pack-dimension without first reading `purchaseDisplay` · **Found by:** CC, `unit_conversions.csv` pre-fill pass.
- **Status:** 🔴 **OPEN** · **Priority:** **P3** · **Target:** rides with the intake block (D-WS9-226) · **Cross-ref:** **D-WS9-222** · **D-WS9-225** · BUG-124.
- **Symptom:** 39 of the 260 rows on the conversion-gap list need no conversion at all — the need unit is a mass and the pack display already states a mass: `bacon` need lb against `1 package (12 oz)`, `crushed tomatoes` need ounce against `1 can (14.5 oz)`, five pasta rows against `1 box (1 lb)`, three cheeses against `1 block (8 oz)`. **`1 oz = 28.3495 g` is arithmetic, not a figure anyone has to supply.**
- ✅ **INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED AT EXACTLY 39, September 8, 2026** — the pre-fill lane's own `_uc_askwrong.txt` sidecar lists **39 rows, every one of the form *"asks grams per oz but oz IS a mass unit."*** **Same count, same rows, reached from the other direction (the audit flagging its own asks as suspect rather than the review flagging the data).** ⚠️ **Two methods agreeing on a count is worth more than either number alone — and this project has been bitten twice by figures that measured something other than their caption.**
- 🔴 **THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER THIS IS A SCRIPT ARTIFACT OR A LIVE RESOLVER BLIND SPOT, AND IT IS UNMEASURED.** The gap detector that produced the asks is audit-side. **If the PRODUCTION resolver shares the blind spot, then 39 live rows fail a conversion that is pure arithmetic; if it does not, the only cost was 39 wasted review rows.** ⚠️ **Measure that before scoping the fix — the two answers are different bugs with different priorities.**
- ✅ **THE FIX IS TO READ THE DISPLAY BEFORE DECLARING A GAP**, which shrinks the human-review surface by 15% at zero judgement cost. ⚠️ **The complement is the real hole and belongs to D-WS9-222: 22 rows carry a pack unit with NO size stated anywhere** — `1 packet` (fajita/taco seasoning: 1 oz or 1.25 oz by brand), `1 container` (salt), **17 herb rows reading `1 bunch`**, `1 head`, and `4 lb pack` for chicken halves with no count. ⚠️ **Every low-confidence figure in `unit_conversions.csv` traces back to that one missing datum.**
